title: A reduced closed subscheme with dense rational points descends
statement: Let $F\subseteq L$ be any extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-field], and let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $F$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Write $X_L=X\times_F L$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $Z\hookrightarrow X_L$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] that is reduced (all its local rings have no nonzero nilpotents). Suppose $S\subseteq X(F)$ is a set of rational points [def-pc-rational-point] such that each base-changed point $s_L$ factors through $Z$, and the images of these points are Zariski dense in $Z$ (every closed subset of $Z$ containing them is all of $Z$). Then there is a unique reduced closed subscheme $Z_F\hookrightarrow X$ for which $(Z_F)_L=Z$ as closed subschemes of $X_L$. The empty subscheme and $S=\varnothing$ are allowed.

source.place: Appendix A.24 and A.28 (closed subschemes and sections of reduced schemes), pp.571–572, and A.65, pp.580–581 (uniqueness of a field model). Agent coefficient-basis argument extending these observations; its full argument is recorded in report.md, not assumed from A.65.

proof.text: Let $T$ be the closure in $X$ of the images of $S$, and let $Y=T_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, write $S_U$ for the members of $S$ landing in $U$, and $I_U$ for the ideal of $Y$ on $U$. The cited node identifies $I_U$ with the functions vanishing at all points of $T\cap U$. Hence $I_U=\bigcap_{s\in S_U}\ker(\operatorname{ev}_s:A\to F)$: one inclusion is immediate; for the other, the zero set of $a\in A$ is closed in $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function], and contains $S_U$, so it contains its closure $T\cap U$. Here closure commutes with restriction to an open, because each neighbourhood of a point of $U$ can be intersected with $U$. The evaluations are $F$-algebra maps, since a rational point is a section and morphisms between affine schemes correspond to ring maps.

source.place: Tag 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), explicit vanishing ideal; Tag 01HZ (lemma-f-open); Milne Appendix A.24 and A.28

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso], $U_L=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=L\otimes_F A$ and projection induced by $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. Write $Z\cap U_L=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J_U)$ using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For $s\in S_U$ its base-changed evaluation is $\operatorname{ev}_{s,L}(\lambda\otimes a)=\lambda\operatorname{ev}_s(a)$ by the tensor pushout universal property. The ideal $J_U$ is exactly the intersection of their kernels. Indeed $J_U$ vanishes on these points by the factorization hypothesis. Conversely, if $b$ vanishes on all these points, its nonvanishing open on $Z\cap U_L$ is empty by density and [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function]. Consequently its image lies in every prime of $B/J_U$, so is nilpotent by [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] with ideal zero; it is zero since this affine open is reduced, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff]. Reducedness here follows directly by restricting the local-ring hypothesis on $Z$. Density restricts to this open by the same neighbourhood argument as in step 1.

Apply [lem-sfb-common-linear-kernel-field-extension] to the $F$-vector space $A$ and the family $(\operatorname{ev}_s)_{s\in S_U}$. Interchanging the tensor factors gives $J_U=\operatorname{span}_L\{1\otimes a:a\in I_U\}$. This span is precisely the ideal generated by $1\otimes I_U$ in $B$: every element of $B$ is a finite sum of pure tensors, and $(\lambda\otimes a)(1\otimes i)=\lambda\otimes ai$ with $ai\in I_U$. Conversely any such $L$-linear combination is in the generated ideal. These multiplication and generation rules are [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the interchange is the linear isomorphism $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes a$, with inverse the same formula, obtained from their bilinear universal property.

source.place: Agent coefficient-basis argument following Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product); compare Tags 059R and 059M for free-module tensor/product injectivity

proof.text: By [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension], the ideal of $Y_L$ on each $U_L$ is generated by $1\otimes I_U$. Thus step 3 identifies it with the ideal $J_U$ of $Z$. These opens cover $X_L$, because they are inverse images of an affine open cover of $X$. The ideal sheaves therefore agree: equality of subsheaves can be checked after restriction to a cover, by the sheaf locality axiom. The affine ideal descriptions and their associated ideal subsheaves are given by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] to obtain the unique isomorphism $Y_L\cong Z$ over $X_L$, which is equality of closed subschemes. Take $Z_F=Y$, already reduced by step 1.

source.place: Appendix A.24 and A.65, pp.571 and 581; affine ideal extension by schemes.tex Tag 01I4 and closed-subscheme uniqueness by Tag 01HO

proof.text: For uniqueness, the projection $W_L\to W$ is surjective for every $F$-scheme $W$: [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective] gives surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] preserves it. If another reduced closed subscheme $Y^{\prime}\hookrightarrow X$ has $Y^{\prime}_L=Z=Y_L$, projecting these two equal images to $X$ gives $|Y^{\prime}|=p(|Z|)=|Y|=T$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] gives $Y^{\prime}=Y$ as closed subschemes. If $S=\varnothing$, density forces $Z$ empty, $T$ is empty and its reduced induced subscheme is empty, so all the preceding steps still apply (intersections over empty families are the whole ring). No separability, perfection, separatedness of $X$, or finite degree of $L/F$ was used.
